[Captured Japanese Documents:] Duty roster for the 238th Infantry Regt Infantry Gun Det [File in Japanese] This item is a duty roster chart from 1942 or 1943. Judging from the names that appear on the chart, it was made for the 238th Infantry Gun Detachment. The chart is filled in with a special code, with different colours and symbols signifying the nature and length of duty for the 115 soldiers named. Some of the names have red lines drawn through them, perhaps indicating hospitalisation or death, and some of the unit were apparently left behind at Palau, although whether this was due to injury or some other reason is uncertain. Two soldiers are also noted at the end of the chart as having been transferred to other units. This item was captured at Finschhafen in 1944.

It belonged to SHIROMIZU Haruo and was probably captured in the Philippines in late 1944 or early 1945. [Captured Japanese Documents:] Army lists of WOs and NCOs from the 20th Division [File in Japanese] This item is a register for the period December 1942-January 1943, of skilled warrant officers and non-commissioned officers attached to the 20th Division. At the beginning of the register is a table explaining the code numbers attached to each regiment and sub-division within the 29th division. These numbers are listed against the name of each officer named in the register, which calculates the number of years of active service for each officer. The register also contains tables of weapons and ordnance assigned to the division and instructions on how the register should be filled in and maintained by senior officers. At the back of the register are regulations concerning the handling and maintenance of weapons and ordnance. This item was probably captured at Finschhafen in April 1944.

[Captured Japanese Documents:] Notification of cipher/code teams for the MAKINO and KUZUME Units [File in Japanese] This item is a fragment of a top secret message dated April 26, 1944, naming the members and duties of special cipher/code teams for two army units called the MAKINO and KUZUME Units. The envelope in which the message was originally contained is also present. This item was captured at Mokmer in June 1944.

[Captured Japanese Documents:] HARADA Masao military pocketbook [File in Japanese] AJRP Sub-Series name: ADVATIS material captured in the Philippines 1944-45 - This item consists of the military pocketbook belonging to HARADA Masao from the Kurume divisional district (Kyushu). It contains extensive exhorations and instructions - including the "Armed services rescript (1882)", the "Field services code (1941)" and "Preparations for mobilisation". It also includes sections for detail of service - such as name - address - unit - height - clothing sizes - academic record - awards and ounishments - injuries and sickness and troop movements. A Japanese soldier was expected to keep this book in good order and up to date. The pocketbook was probably captured in the Philippines in  late 1944 or early 1945.

[Captured Japanese Documents - Imperial Japanese Army] Morse code mnemonic chart - AJRP Sub-Series name: ATIS material registered as A documents - This item consists of a mnemonic chart for Morse code published by Senryudo in Tokyo in 1939. It contains instructions to Morse signallers - and a Morse conversion chart for the English alphabet and the Japanese syllablry. For example - the Japanese syllable "ha" is represented by dash-dot-dot-dot - with the mnemonic "harmonice" (pronounced haa-mo-ni-ka). This item would have been of immediate interest to the Allies - as indicated by its classification as an "A" document.
